title: Śrī Śrī Upadeśāmṛta
author: by Śrīla Rūpa Goswāmī Prabhu in Sanskrit
subtitle: Verse Seven

text: kintv ādarād anudinaṁ khalu saiva juṣṭā
translation: The Holy Name, Character, Pastimes and Activities of Kṛṣṇa are all transcendentally sweet like sugar candy. Although the tongue of one afflicted by the jaundice of avidyā (ignorance) cannot taste anything sweet, it is wonderful that simply by carefully chanting these sweet Names every day, a natural relish awakens within one’s tongue, and one’s disease is gradually destroyed at the root.
*Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur’s corresponding Bengali composition:*
There is no taste for chanting about Kṛṣṇa on a tongue that is defiled by the jaundice of ignorance. Alas!
Like sugar candy, daily engaging in discussion of Kṛṣṇa with faith produces genuine ruchi.
The root of the disease – ignorance, forgetfulness that Kṛṣṇa is our desired end – is gradually uprooted by chanting about Kṛṣṇa.
By chanting, the taste of Kṛṣṇa’s Name, Pastimes, and so on, increases day by day, and one’s ruchi becomes constant.
